mainTopic: The end of the משנה about the six customs of the people of יריחו, a ברייתא about six actions of חזקיה המלך, and the גמרא's explanation of how the people of יריחו grafted palm trees (מרכיבין דקלים).
overview: This amud opens with the end of the משנה, which finishes listing the customs of the people of יריחו that the חכמים protested. The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same three-and-three pattern: six actions of חזקיה המלך, three the חכמים agreed with and three they did not. It then explains two of יריחו's customs. Grafting palms is either pouring a special mixture into the tree (רב יהודה) or placing a male branch on a female palm (רב אחא בריה דרבא). 'Bundling שמע' gets several explanations: not pausing, pausing in the wrong place, or leaving out ברוך שם. That leads to the question of why we say ברוך שם at all. ריש לקיש answers with the story of יעקב and his sons, and the חכמים rule that it is said quietly. רבי אבהו adds that it was said aloud where מינים might complain. Finally, a ברייתא records the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה on how to classify the six customs of יריחו. The amud ends with a challenge to רבי יהודה from a משנה about harvesting before the עומר, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The last customs of יריחו that the חכמים protested
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of three customs of the people of יריחו that the חכמים protested: eating fallen fruit on שבת and giving פאה from vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they would eat fruit that fell from beneath the trees on שבת, and they would give פאה from vegetables. And the חכמים protested against them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the tail end of the משנה. It completes the list of three things the people of יריחו did that the חכמים protested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה listed three customs of יריחו that the חכמים let pass. One of them was grafting palm trees all day on ערב פסח. It then began a second list of three that the חכמים protested. These last two items finish that second list. The problems are that fruit falling on שבת may be מוקצה, and that vegetables are exempt from פאה altogether. The גמרא explains these concerns later.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit that falls off the tree by itself (here, from trees that shed their fruit)
The corner of the field left for the poor
Vegetables, which are exempt from פאה
They protested against them; they objected
The core text that the גמרא explains

phrases.english: and they would eat from beneath the trees that shed fruit on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Concern: the fruit may have fallen on שבת itself and be מוקצה.

phrases.english: and they would give the corner-gift to the poor from vegetables.
phrases.notes: Vegetables are exempt from פאה.

phrases.english: And the Sages protested against them.
phrases.notes: Applies to all three items in this second list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's second list (the protested customs) begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים protested against eating fallen fruit on שבת and against giving פאה from vegetables.

steps.title: Six actions of חזקיה המלך: the three the חכמים agreed with
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists six actions of חזקיה המלך. It begins with the three the חכמים agreed with.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: King חזקיה did six things. The חכמים agreed with him on three and did not agree with him on three. He dragged his father's bones on a bed of ropes, and they agreed. He crushed the copper snake, and they agreed. He hid away the Book of Cures, and they agreed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא. Like our משנה, it splits six actions into three that were accepted and three that were not. Here we get the three that were accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no question or challenge here. The ברייתא is brought because its pattern (six actions, three approved, three rejected) matches the משנה about יריחו. Each approved action removed something harmful. Dragging the bones of his wicked father אחז publicly shamed him. The נחש הנחשת had become an object of עבודה זרה. The ספר רפואות made people rely on cures instead of praying to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: They agreed with him; they approved
The copper snake that משה made in the desert
He hid away, put out of use

steps.confusionAlert: הודו לו does not mean 'they thanked him.' It means the חכמים agreed with what he did.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: King Hezekiah did six things;
on three they agreed with him,
and on three they did not agree with him:
he dragged the bones of his father
phrases.notes: His father was the wicked King אחז.

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִטָּה שֶׁל חֲבָלִים — וְהוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: on a bed of ropes, and they agreed with him.
phrases.notes: Instead of a royal funeral.

phrases.english: He crushed the copper snake, and they agreed with him.
phrases.notes: People had been worshipping it.

phrases.english: He hid away the Book of Cures, and they agreed with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה דְבָרִים עָשָׂה חִזְקִיָּה הַמֶּלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא with the same structure as the משנה (three approved, three protested).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים approved three actions of חזקיה: shaming his father's burial, crushing the נחש הנחשת, and hiding the ספר רפואות.

steps.title: The three actions of חזקיה the חכמים did not agree with
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes with the three actions of חזקיה that the חכמים rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: On three they did not agree with him. He cut off the doors of the היכל and sent them to the king of אשור, and they did not agree. He blocked the waters of the upper גיחון, and they did not agree. He made the year a leap year in ניסן, during ניסן itself, and they did not agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the second half of its list: the three actions of חזקיה that the חכמים did not approve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each rejected action had a flaw. Cutting the doors off the היכל disgraced the בית המקדש. Blocking the גיחון spring showed a lack of trust in ה׳ and hurt the local people. Adding a leap month once ניסן had already begun was improper, because the decision to add a month (עיבור השנה) must be made before ניסן starts.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש
The upper Gihon spring near ירושלים
He made the year a leap year by adding a month

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה did six things: the חכמים agreed with three (his father's bones, the copper snake, the Book of Cures) and disagreed with three (the היכל doors, the Gihon, the leap year in ניסן). This parallels the משנה's split of the six customs of יריחו.

phrases.english: And on three they did not agree with him:
he cut off the doors of the Sanctuary

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁיגְּרָן לְמֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר — וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: and sent them to the king of Assyria, and they did not agree with him.

phrases.aramaic: סָתַם מֵי גִיחוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן — וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: He blocked the waters of the upper Gihon, and they did not agree with him.

phrases.aramaic: עִיבֵּר נִיסָן בְּנִיסָן — וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: He made a leap year in Nisan during Nisan, and they did not agree with him.
phrases.notes: He declared the day that should have been ניסן to be another day of אדר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים rejected three actions of חזקיה: sending the היכל doors to אשור, blocking the Gihon, and adding a leap month during ניסן.

steps.title: How did they graft the palm trees?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's statement that the people of יריחו grafted palm trees all day on ערב פסח, and asks how this was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: they grafted palm trees the whole day. How did they do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks a practical question about it. This sets up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge to the משנה. It is a request for information about what 'grafting palm trees' actually involved. The answers below describe the farming technique.

keyTerms.meaning: They graft or treat trees to help them grow and bear fruit

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] They graft palm trees the entire day, etc.
phrases.notes: This refers to the 14th of ניסן (ערב פסח).

phrases.english: How did they do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חזקיה ברייתא and returns to explain an item from the משנה's first list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the actual technique of 'grafting palm trees' mentioned in the משנה?

steps.title: רב יהודה: pouring a special mixture into the palm
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that they boiled a mixture of fresh myrtle, laurel beer and fresh barley flour, then poured it into the heart of the palm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: They brought fresh myrtle, beer made from laurel, and barley flour that had been put into a vessel less than forty days earlier. They boiled these together and poured the mixture into the heart of the palm tree. Any tree standing within four אמות of it that was not treated the same way would wither right away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by describing a recipe that was poured into the palm tree to make it flourish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this explanation, 'grafting' does not mean attaching branches. It means feeding the tree a strong boiled mixture. The treatment was so powerful that untreated trees within four אמות would dry up immediately, because the treated tree drew strength away from them.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
They bring fresh myrtle,
and beer made from laurel,
and barley flour
that was put into a vessel
over which forty days have not yet passed,
phrases.notes: The flour must be fresh.

phrases.english: and they boil them,
and pour them into the palm tree, into its heart,
and any [tree] that stands within its four cubits,
if they do not do this to it as well,
it withers immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מַיְיתֵי אָסָא דָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Grafting means pouring a boiled mixture of fresh myrtle, laurel beer and fresh barley flour into the heart of the palm.

steps.title: רב אחא son of רבא: placing a male palm branch on a female
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא gives a different explanation: they placed a branch of a male palm onto a female palm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, said: They place a branch of the male palm on the female palm.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another answer to the same question: the grafting was pollination, done by placing a male palm branch on a female tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה understood the work as feeding the tree. רב אחא בריה דרבא understands it as pollination, which makes the female palm bear fruit. Both are answering the same question about what the משנה's 'grafting' involved.

keyTerms.meaning: A branch or flower cluster of the palm

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of 'grafting palms' in the משנה. רב יהודה says they poured a special boiled mixture into the tree. רב אחא בריה דרבא says they placed a male palm branch on a female palm.

phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said:
They place a branch of the male palm on the female.
phrases.notes: This is pollination, so the female tree bears fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר: מַנְּחִי כּוּפְרָא דִּיכְרָא לְנוּקְבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question that רב יהודה answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Grafting means pollinating the female palm with a branch of the male palm.

steps.title: What does 'bundling שמע' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next custom of the people of יריחו from the משנה, that they 'bundled' שמע, and asks what they actually did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they bundle שמע.' How did they do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up another phrase from the משנה and asks what it means. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used an unclear word, כורכין ('bundling' or 'wrapping together'), without explaining it. The גמרא wants to know what this 'bundling' looked like in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Bundling or wrapping together (here: running the words of שמע together)

phrases.english: And they bundle Shema.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה about the people of יריחו.

phrases.english: How did they do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 4: the גמרא returns to the משנה and explains the next custom of יריחו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the people of יריחו did when they 'bundled' שמע.

steps.title: רב יהודה: they did not pause
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says they said the first פסוק of שמע and did not make the proper pause.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: They said 'שמע ישראל ה׳ אלקינו ה׳ אחד' and did not pause.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the first explanation of 'bundling': they ran the words together without stopping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יהודה, the 'bundle' was about timing. They said the words correctly but skipped the pause that should be made, so the words were 'wrapped together'.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who gives the first explanation

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרִים ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד״,
phrases.english: They would say: 'Hear Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One,'
and they would not pause.
phrases.notes: Many explain: no break after אחד before continuing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Bundling' means saying שמע without making the necessary pause.

steps.title: רבא: they paused in the wrong place
steps.stepSummary: רבא says they did pause, but in the wrong spot, so the פסוק came out sounding like 'today on your heart, and not tomorrow'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They did pause, but they said 'today on your heart', which implies: today it is on your heart, and tomorrow it is not on your heart.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation of 'bundling'. The problem was not a missing pause but a pause in the wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'אשר אנכי מצוך היום / על לבבך', meaning 'which I command you today, shall be on your heart'. By attaching היום to על לבבך, it sounds like the מצוה applies only today. So they 'bundled' words that should have been kept apart.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who disagrees with רב יהודה
'Today on your heart', a wrong grouping of the פסוק's words

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is NOT saying they skipped a pause. He agrees they paused, but it came in the wrong place, which changed the meaning.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They did pause,
but they would say 'today on your heart',
phrases.notes: They joined היום to the next words instead of the words before it.

phrases.english: which implies: today it is on your heart,
and not tomorrow on your heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 7 that disagrees with רב יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Bundling' means pausing in the wrong place, so היום is joined to על לבבך.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי מאיר says they did not pause
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks the same question and records רבי מאיר's view: they said the פסוק without pausing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: How did they bundle שמע? They said 'שמע ישראל ה׳ אלקינו ה׳ אחד' and did not pause. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same topic. Its first opinion, from רבי מאיר, matches רב יהודה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the question of 'bundling' was already debated by תנאים. רבי מאיר's wording is the same as רב יהודה's, so רב יהודה is following רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the words of רבי מאיר

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
How would they bundle Shema?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרִים ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד״,
phrases.english: They would say: 'Hear Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One,'
and they would not pause,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד הָיוּ כּוֹרְכִין אֶת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא whose first opinion matches רב יהודה in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: 'bundling' means saying the פסוק without pausing.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: they paused but skipped ברוך שם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה in the ברייתא says they did pause, but they did not say ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: They did pause, but they did not say 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד'.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion in the ברייתא gives a new meaning to 'bundling': leaving out ברוך שם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the 'bundle' was that they went straight from the פסוק of שמע to the next part without saying ברוך שם in between. This brings up ברוך שם for the first time, which leads to the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: תנא who disagrees with רבי מאיר

keyTerms.term: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
keyTerms.meaning: 'Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever', said after the first פסוק of שמע

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse רבי יהודה (the תנא here) with רב יהודה (the אמורא in Step 8). They are different people with different explanations.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They did pause,
but they would not say
'Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion in the same ברייתא, disagreeing with רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: 'bundling' means not saying ברוך שם after the פסוק of שמע.

steps.title: Why do we say ברוך שם at all?
steps.stepSummary: Since ברוך שם is not in the תורה's text of שמע, the גמרא asks why we say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we, why do we say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we add ברוך שם when it is not written in the פרשה. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treated leaving out ברוך שם as a mistake. That raises a question: if the words are not written in the פרשה of שמע, where does our practice of saying them come from?

phrases.english: And we, what is the reason we say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prompted by רבי יהודה's mention of ברוך שם.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for adding ברוך שם, which is not in the פסוקים.

steps.title: Answer: ריש לקיש's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we say it because of a דרשה of רבי שמעון בן לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמעון בן לקיש expounded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer that points to a teaching it is about to quote. This is a setup for the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is not a פסוק but a דרשה. The full teaching comes in the next steps.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish expounded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by pointing to ריש לקיש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We say ברוך שם because of ריש לקיש's דרשה.

steps.title: יעקב loses prophecy before revealing the End
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains a פסוק: יעקב wanted to tell his sons when the final redemption would come, but the שכינה left him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As ריש לקיש said: 'And יעקב called his sons and said: Gather, and I will tell you.' יעקב wanted to reveal to his sons the End of Days, and the שכינה left him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins ריש לקיש's story. יעקב was about to share a secret prophecy and suddenly lost it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says יעקב would tell his sons what would happen 'in the end of days', but the blessings that follow never say this. ריש לקיש explains that the שכינה departed, so יעקב could not reveal it.

keyTerms.meaning: The End of Days, the time of the final redemption
The Divine Presence (here: the spirit of prophecy)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
'And Jacob called his sons'
'and said: Gather, and I will tell you.'
phrases.notes: בראשית מט:א

phrases.aramaic: בִּיקֵּשׁ יַעֲקֹב לְגַלּוֹת לְבָנָיו קֵץ הַיָּמִין,
phrases.english: Jacob wanted to reveal to his sons the End of Days,
and the Divine Presence departed from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching that Step 13 referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב wanted to reveal the End, but the שכינה left him.

steps.title: יעקב fears one of his sons is unworthy
steps.stepSummary: יעקב worries that the שכינה left because one of his children is unfit, like ישמעאל from אברהם and עשו from יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid, there is someone unfit among my children, like אברהם, from whom ישמעאל came, and my father יצחק, from whom עשו came?
steps.whatsHappening: יעקב tries to understand why he lost prophecy. He fears a flaw in his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב uses family history as his reasoning: both his grandfather and his father had a child who strayed. So he suspects the same thing happened to him.

keyTerms.meaning: In my bed, meaning among my children

phrases.english: He said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid,
there is something unfit in my bed (among my children),
like Abraham, from whom Ishmael came,
and my father Isaac, from whom Esau came?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: יעקב reacts to losing the שכינה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב suspects one of his children is unworthy.

steps.title: The sons answer: שמע ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The sons reassure יעקב (whose name is ישראל) by saying שמע ישראל: just as you have only one God in your heart, so do we.
steps.simpleTranslation: His sons said to him: 'Hear, ישראל, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One.' They said: Just as in your heart there is only One, so in our hearts there is only One.
steps.whatsHappening: The sons answer their father's fear by declaring their faith, addressing him as 'ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'ישראל' means יעקב himself, not the Jewish people. The sons are telling him: 'Listen, father ישראל, ה׳ is our God too.' Their declaration sets up יעקב's response in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as in your heart there is only One

steps.confusionAlert: In this story, 'ישראל' in שמע ישראל is the name of יעקב, the person being spoken to, not the nation.

phrases.english: His sons said to him:
'Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ אֶלָּא אֶחָד,
phrases.english: They said: Just as in your heart there is only One,
so too in our hearts there is only One.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The sons respond to יעקב's worry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sons declare their complete faith using the words of שמע ישראל.

steps.title: יעקב responds with ברוך שם
steps.stepSummary: Relieved, יעקב answers: ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד. This is the source for saying it after שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that moment יעקב אבינו began and said: 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד.'
steps.whatsHappening: יעקב replies to his sons with words of praise. This completes the answer to why we say ברוך שם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons said שמע and יעקב responded with ברוך שם. That is why we follow שמע with ברוך שם. It comes from יעקב's response, not from the פסוקים written by משה.
steps.whatToRemember: יעקב's sons declared שמע ישראל to him, and ברוך שם was יעקב's response. That is why we say ברוך שם after the first פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה פָּתַח יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: At that moment Jacob our father began and said:
'Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: יעקב responds to his sons; this completes the answer to Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב said ברוך שם in response to שמע, which is the source of our custom.

steps.title: The dilemma: משה didn't say it, יעקב did
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are unsure whether to say ברוך שם, since משה did not include it in the תורה but יעקב said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said: What should we do? Should we say it? משה רבינו did not say it. Should we not say it? יעקב said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים lay out a problem with two sides: there is a reason to say ברוך שם and a reason not to. This sets up their solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two pulls. Since it is not in the פרשה משה wrote, adding it seems wrong. Since יעקב said it as a response to שמע, leaving it out also seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: משה our teacher, who wrote the פרשה of שמע in the תורה

phrases.english: The Rabbis said: What should we do?
Should we say it? Moses our teacher did not say it.
Should we not say it? Jacob said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the story: now the חכמים must decide how to treat ברוך שם in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ברוך שם should be said, since it has a source in יעקב but is not in משה's text.

steps.title: The ruling: say it quietly
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים decided that ברוך שם should be said silently, which solves the dilemma.
steps.simpleTranslation: They instituted that people should say it quietly.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים settle the dilemma with a middle path: say ברוך שם, but quietly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying it honors יעקב's words. Saying it quietly shows it is not part of the written text of משה. Both concerns are addressed.
steps.whatToRemember: We say ברוך שם quietly because it comes from יעקב and not from the פסוקים of משה. It is a compromise between saying it and leaving it out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the practice to whisper ברוך שם after the first פסוק of שמע.

phrases.english: They instituted that they should say it quietly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the dilemma of Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ברוך שם is said, but quietly.

steps.title: Parable of the king's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי אמי explains the quiet ruling with a parable: a princess craves a lowly food, so her servants bring it to her quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said that the school of רבי אמי said: This is like a king's daughter who smelled the spicy food stuck to a pot. If she asks for it, it is embarrassing for her. If she does not ask, she suffers. So her servants began to bring it to her quietly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a parable that pictures the חכמים' ruling of saying ברוך שם quietly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking openly would bring embarrassment, and not asking would bring suffering. Bringing it quietly avoids both problems. In the same way, saying ברוך שם aloud would look like adding to משה's text, and skipping it would lose יעקב's praise, so it is said quietly.

keyTerms.meaning: Bits of spiced food stuck to the bottom of a pot

steps.whyThisMatters: The parable shows a general way to handle a two-sided problem: find a quiet middle path that respects both concerns.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said that the school of Rabbi Ami said:
It is like a king's daughter
who smelled the spiced food stuck to a pot.
If she says so (asks for it), it is a disgrace for her.
If she does not say so, she suffers.
Her servants began to bring it quietly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the quiet ruling of Step 19 with a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Just as the servants quietly bring the princess what she wants, ברוך שם is said quietly to avoid both problems.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: The custom was changed to say it aloud
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports that the חכמים instituted saying ברוך שם out loud because of complaints from the מינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: They instituted that people should say it out loud, because of the complaints of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו adds a later development to the silent ruling from Step 19. The חכמים switched to saying ברוך שם out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Jews whispered a line in the middle of שמע, the מינים could claim they were secretly saying something improper. So the חכמים had it said aloud, which removed the grounds for that accusation. The reason is about outside suspicion, not about the line itself.

keyTerms.meaning: They instituted (an enactment of the חכמים)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ אוֹמְרִים אוֹתוֹ בְּקוֹל רָם,
phrases.english: They instituted that people should say it out loud,
phrases.notes: "It" means ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד.

phrases.english: because of the complaints of the heretics.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ אוֹמְרִים אוֹתוֹ בְּקוֹל רָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a later enactment that modifies the silent ruling explained in Steps 19-20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברוך שם was instituted to be said aloud to avoid the מינים' accusations.

steps.title: In נהרדעא they still say it quietly
steps.stepSummary: In נהרדעא, where there are no מינים, people still say ברוך שם quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in נהרדעא, where there are no מינים, until now they say it quietly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the change to saying it aloud depended on where people lived. Where there were no מינים, the original quiet custom stayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that the loud custom was only a response to the מינים. Where that reason did not apply, the basic quiet ruling stayed in place.

keyTerms.meaning: נהרדעא, a major Jewish city in בבל

steps.whatToRemember: ברוך שם is basically said quietly (Step 19). It was said aloud only where מינים might accuse Jews of something, and in נהרדעא it stayed quiet.

phrases.english: And in Nehardea, where there are no heretics,
until now they say it quietly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי אבהו's enactment to places where מינים are present.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without מינים, the original quiet practice continues.

steps.title: A ברייתא introduces six customs of the people of יריחו
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the people of יריחו did six things: three with the חכמים' approval and three without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: The people of יריחו did six things. Three were with the approval of the חכמים, and three were without the approval of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא brings a new ברייתא and gives its headline before listing the actual customs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is the full תנאי dispute behind our משנה's list of six customs of יריחו. רבי מאיר divides them into approved and unapproved. רבי יהודה divides them into tolerated and protested. Our משנה's wording ('ומיחו בידם חכמים', with פאה from vegetables in the protested group) matches רבי יהודה's version.

keyTerms.meaning: With the approval of the חכמים

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The people of Jericho did six things,
three with the approval of the Sages,
and three without the approval of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים עָשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי יְרִיחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's six customs of יריחו and brings the ברייתא in which רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה dispute how to classify them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of יריחו had six notable customs, split three and three.

steps.title: The three customs the Sages approved (according to רבי מאיר)
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, the approved customs were grafting palms all day, running שמע together, and harvesting before the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these were with the approval of the חכמים: They grafted palm trees the whole day, they ran שמע together, and they harvested before the עומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists the first group of three. These are customs the חכמים agreed with, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grafting palms "all day" means all of ערב פסח, the 14th of ניסן, even after midday. This list is רבי מאיר's, and in Step 10 רבי מאיר explained כורכין את שמע as saying the פסוק without pausing (leaving out ברוך שם is רבי יהודה's view, from Step 11). Here harvesting before the עומר is counted as approved, and the משנה quoted in Step 30 agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Running שמע together without the usual pauses
The barley offering of ט״ז ניסן. New grain may not be harvested or eaten before it.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think כורכין את שמע means they skipped שמע. They said it, but in an irregular way. The גמרא already explained what that way was in Steps 7-11, and the explanations differ.

phrases.english: And these were with the approval of the Sages:
they grafted palm trees the whole day,
phrases.notes: The whole day of ערב פסח, even after midday.

phrases.english: and they ran Shema together,
and they harvested before the Omer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the ברייתא's headline.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grafting all day, כורכין את שמע, and harvesting before the עומר were approved (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: The three customs the Sages did not approve (according to רבי מאיר)
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, the unapproved customs were piling grain before the עומר, opening fences for the poor on שבת, and using branches of הקדש trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these were without the approval of the חכמים: They piled grain before the עומר. They broke openings in the fences of their gardens and orchards so the poor could eat fallen fruit in drought years, on שבת and יום טוב. And they permitted the branches of consecrated carob and sycamore trees. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists the second group of three and names רבי מאיר as the author of this version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Piling the harvest is a bigger action than just cutting it, so רבי מאיר saw it as going too far before the עומר. Letting the poor take fruit that fell on שבת or יום טוב was a problem because such fruit may not be eaten that day. Their ancestors had dedicated these trees to הקדש. The people of יריחו claimed the dedication covered only the trunks, so they used the newer branches, and the חכמים disagreed.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit that fell from the tree
Branches of trees dedicated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And these were without the approval of the Sages:
they piled grain before the Omer,
and they broke openings in their gardens and orchards
to let the poor eat fallen fruit
in drought years, on Shabbat and Yom Tov,
and they permitted consecrated branches
of carob and of sycamore trees,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי מאיר's version of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Piling before the עומר, opening fences for the poor on שבת, and using הקדש branches were against the חכמים' wishes (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: רבי יהודה objects: Then why only יריחו?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argues that if the חכמים approved these customs, everyone would do them, so it makes no sense to single out יריחו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: If they were doing it with the approval of the Sages, then everyone would do the same.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה challenges how רבי מאיר set up the list. Calling something "approved" doesn't fit with treating it as a special custom of יריחו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא presents these as things unique to יריחו. If the חכמים fully approved them, the whole Jewish people would do them and there would be nothing to report about יריחו. So רבי יהודה argues the "approved" category can't be right.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
If they were doing it with the approval of the Sages,
then everyone would do the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אִם בִּרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the premise of רבי מאיר's first category.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's claim that three customs were done with the חכמים' approval.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fully approved practice would be universal, so it would not be a special custom of יריחו worth recording.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's new framework: all against the Sages' wishes, but only three protested
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says all six went against the חכמים' wishes. The difference is that the חכמים protested three and let three go.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both groups were done without the approval of the Sages. About three the Sages protested against them, and about three they did not protest against them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה replaces רבי מאיר's categories with a new way of dividing the six customs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dividing line is no longer "approved or not approved." It becomes "protested or tolerated." The חכמים disliked all six, but for three of them the case was arguable, so they did not openly stop the people of יריחו.
steps.confusionAlert: "לא מיחו" (they did not protest) does not mean the חכמים approved. In רבי יהודה's view, they disapproved of all six but chose not to fight over three.

phrases.english: Rather, both these and those
they were doing without the approval of the Sages,
about three they protested against them,
and about three they did not protest against them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers רבי יהודה's corrected framework after his objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three customs were fully approved by the חכמים (רבי מאיר).
steps.terutzMaskana: None were approved. The only difference is whether the חכמים protested.

steps.title: The three customs the Sages tolerated (according to רבי יהודה)
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, the חכמים did not protest grafting all day, running שמע together, or harvesting and piling before the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the ones they did not protest: They grafted palm trees the whole day, they ran שמע together, and they harvested and piled grain before the עומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה lists the customs the חכמים let go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is one important shift from רבי מאיר. Piling (גודשין) is moved into the tolerated group together with harvesting. That frees up a slot, which רבי יהודה fills with a new custom in the next step.

phrases.english: And these are the ones they did not protest:
they grafted palm trees the whole day,
and they ran Shema together,
and they harvested and piled grain before the Omer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of רבי יהודה's framework.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grafting all day, כורכין את שמע, and harvesting plus piling were tolerated (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: The three customs the Sages protested (according to רבי יהודה)
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, the חכמים protested using הקדש branches, opening fences for the poor on שבת, and giving פאה from vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the ones they protested: They permitted the consecrated branches of carob and sycamore trees. They broke openings in their gardens and orchards so the poor could eat fallen fruit on שבת and יום טוב in drought years. They gave פאה from vegetables. And the חכמים protested against them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה finishes his list with the three customs the חכמים actively protested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two items are the same as רבי מאיר's "unapproved" list. The new third item is giving פאה from vegetables. Vegetables are exempt from פאה, so the poor might think this produce is real פאה and wrongly treat it as exempt from מעשרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving פאה (the corner of the field for the poor) from vegetables

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: three customs approved, three not. רבי יהודה: all six were disapproved, three tolerated and three protested. He moves piling into the tolerated group and adds פאה from vegetables to the protested group.

phrases.english: And these are the ones they protested:
they permitted consecrated branches
of carob and of sycamore trees,
and they broke openings in their gardens and orchards
to let the poor eat fallen fruit
on Shabbat and Yom Tov in drought years,
they gave Peah from vegetables,
and the Sages protested against them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהודה's version of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים protested using הקדש branches, opening fences on שבת for fallen fruit, and giving פאה from vegetables (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: Was the harvesting really against the Sages' will?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה. A משנה says the people of יריחו harvested before the עומר with the חכמים' approval. Only their piling of grain was unapproved, and it was not protested.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that the harvesting was against the will of the חכמים? But we learned in a משנה: The people of יריחו harvest before the עומר with the approval of the חכמים. They pile the grain before the עומר without the approval of the חכמים, but the חכמים did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יהודה's claim from Step 27 that harvesting before the עומר was against the חכמים' wishes. It quotes a משנה that clearly says the harvesting was approved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 27-28, רבי יהודה grouped 'harvesting and piling' together as one unprotested custom that was still against the חכמים' will. This משנה splits the two activities. Harvesting was fully approved, and only piling was unapproved but tolerated. That seems to contradict רבי יהודה's version.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But didn't we learn in a משנה?' This phrase introduces a source used to challenge a statement.
Piling the cut grain into stacks (גְּדִישָׁה).
With the approval or consent of the חכמים.
They protested against them, meaning they stopped or rebuked them.

steps.confusionAlert: Keep two separate activities apart. Harvesting (קצירה) means cutting the grain. Piling (גדישה) means stacking it afterward. The משנה treats them differently: harvesting was approved, while piling was unapproved but not protested. Step 28 had combined them into one item.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge forces the גמרא to explain how רבי יהודה's list fits with the משנה. That explanation will be the next move in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold
phrases.notes: A question that is really a challenge.

phrases.english: that harvesting is against the will of the Sages?
phrases.notes: This refers back to Step 27-28, where harvesting was counted among the customs that went against the Sages' wishes.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: This introduces the source for the challenge.

phrases.english: The people of Jericho harvest before the omer
with the will of the Sages,
phrases.notes: This is the key point of the challenge: harvesting was approved.

phrases.english: and they pile the grain before the omer
against the will of the Sages,
but the Sages did not protest against them.
phrases.notes: This wording echoes רבי יהודה's language of 'did not protest.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה קְצִירָה שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים הִיא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's list from Steps 27-28 using a משנה that treats harvesting as approved.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that harvesting before the עומר was against the חכמים' will
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה states that harvesting before the עומר was done with the חכמים' approval. Only piling was unapproved, and it went unprotested. This contradicts listing harvesting as unapproved.
